body:
This updates our existing open PR #299 to record **C68 >= 0.447*, candidate, unrefereed**, replacing its 0.44685 signed-contact draft. It updates `constants/68a.md`, the README bound and recent progress, retaining all existing historical rows and everyone else's bounds.

Credit comes first to **V. Patankar**, whose [PR #274](https://github.com/teorth/optimizationproblems/pull/274) supplies the retained Green/flux input and enclosing framework and states 0.446, with a supplementary certificate at 0.44605; then to **Chunjie Wang** for the [coefficient approach](https://doi.org/10.1090/proc/17112), **Frank Wikström** for [moment integration](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.17748), and our [earlier signed-contact step](https://github.com/rpinho/math-certificates/tree/848f899c973666f64b73fb6f37760849a600285f/c68/signed-contact). Patankar's PR remains open and should be credited before this continuation if it merges. This draft does not add or alter his pending row. No novelty, exhaustive priority or optimality claim is made. Some older files in our certificate repository name the #274 author wrongly as D. Niedbala Giraudin, a different author; [CREDIT_CORRECTION.md](https://github.com/rpinho/math-certificates/blob/09c84234137d3fadee1620dbc1c2ca58d2756ce2/c68/CREDIT_CORRECTION.md) overrides them, and this packet credits V. Patankar.

The candidate uses **c = 447/1000**, exceeding the preceding 8937/20000 by exactly 3/20000. The proposed norm implication is: for every f,u in the Bergman space A²(D), domination |f| <= |u| on 447/1000 < |z| < 1 implies ||f||₂ <= ||u||₂.

The change retains each balancing contact row before averaging. With a = |m₁| and q₀ the second contact moment in its direction, the support inequality (X+1)(M-X) >= 0 yields J = a(q₀+a)/(1+a). The weight becomes max(S,J,T), keeping the joint first/second harmonics and their relative phase. The contact moment PSD condition and an outer-factor Schur complement give a uniform linear-coefficient correction 23/200 = 0.115, replacing 19/200 = 0.095. Only coefficient one is asserted; no half-actual-diameter claim is used.

**What is computation:** the frozen eight-atom rational measure plus Lebesgue tail on [99/100,1] passes a fresh 320-bit exact/Arb replay on the release copy. It checks ordinary moments k=1,...,5999 and weighted moments k=1,...,1799, then both analytic infinite-tail inequalities starting at 6000 and 1800. Minimum relative margins exceed 7.86562e-6 and 7.68082e-6; the first exact tail gap is 33/200000 and the second exceeds 8.88107e-10. The checker reconstructs the complete scalar cover: 265 grid, 17 PSD, four constant and one small leaf. All 35 corrupted artifacts reject with their exact expected codes. Retained counterexamples and exact contact/auxiliary controls also pass. Additional arithmetic replays use mpmath.iv scalar cells and exact integer ordinary moments with a 5000-cell interval integral envelope; their fresh receipts are linked below. No search or optimizer is run for acceptance.

**What is prose:** the Green/flux normalization and exhaustion, minimal contact-disk geometry, new contact-row reduction, outer-function argument and final Bergman norm implication are written analytic arguments. The programs certify their quantitative hypotheses and coverage, not those analytic steps. The source's two-radius attempts and large diagnostic screens are exploratory history, not certificates for an additional claim. The old relaxed .105 counterexample is retained, and its moments are PSD; it is not discarded by an unsupported realizability assumption. The naive third-diagonal extension still fails by exactly -1/100. The same frozen measure fails the full old .095 weighted k=1 condition; this is a comparison for that measure, without a barrier claim for other measures.

An adversarial referee on a different model (GPT-6 Astra), told to break the claim and writing its own interval code, checked the definition match, the contact-row lemma (with a 200,000-configuration counterexample hunt, including the retained .105 and third-coefficient failures), the 23/200 Schur-complement correction, every finite moment and the whole scalar cover, and whether any old-setting lemma was reused. Its verdict was HOLDS, with no mathematical defect found. [Referee report](https://github.com/rpinho/math-certificates/blob/09c84234137d3fadee1620dbc1c2ca58d2756ce2/c68/review/REFEREE.md). This is an AI review, not a second party.

**Verification level: L0** for the bound as a whole (definitions: https://github.com/rpinho/math-certificates/blob/59eeb7097f806da05187b5f234445be3589204d4/VERIFICATION_LEVELS.md)
The verifiers were separately written by the same AI agent; the new contact-row lemma is a prose argument needing mathematical review.

AI use and author review: Analysis and proof drafting by AI agents under my direction; I reviewed the results at summary level. AI agents also prepared the certificates, checkers and submission text. This does not claim a line-by-line human verification. The preceding signed-contact packet had an AI review with separate arithmetic checks; that review does not constitute acceptance of the new contact-row proof or this release. No human referee or proof-assistant formalization is claimed.

No certificate artifacts are added to optimizationproblems.

The live 68a page and upstream main at `87b4ebbd426ff8db597a2004cc45da17903bdcf2` still show 0.432* and Wikström's preceding 0.4263. All 58 open PR file lists and bodies were checked on 4 November 2026: only [#274](https://github.com/teorth/optimizationproblems/pull/274) and [#299](https://github.com/teorth/optimizationproblems/pull/299) change `constants/68a.md`; both remain open. [#223](https://github.com/teorth/optimizationproblems/pull/223) is closed and its Wikström row is already present. The bounded source audit and refreshed public result catalogs located no stronger applicable candidate. Full original Wang access remained unavailable in the source research; the retained explicit derivations and Wikström's paper are available. This is not a global priority finding.

**Models:** GPT-6.1 Sol via Codex (search, proof drafting, certificates, checkers, packaging); GPT-6 Astra (adversarial referee and review); Claude Opus 5.5 via Claude Science (review); Claude Code with Claude Opus 5.5 (coordination).
